blocks.text: The URL Filtering policy consists of rules that you define. When you add a rule, you specify criteria, such as URL categories, users, groups, departments, locations, and time intervals. There is also a recommended policy for URL Filtering.
To allow granular control of filtering, the service organizes URLs into a hierarchy of categories. To learn more about URL categories, see About URL Categories.

By default, the Cloud App Control policy takes precedence over the URL Filtering policy. The service applies the Cloud App Control policy to a web transaction before applying the URL Filtering policy. To change this setting and have the service apply the URL Filtering policy even if it has already applied a Cloud App Control policy, go to Advanced Settings and enable Allow Cascading to URL Filtering. To learn more about the order in which the service enforces all policies, including this policy, see Understanding Policy Enforcement.
URL Filtering provides the following benefits and enables you to:

blocks.item: Limit exposure to liability by managing access to web content based on a site's categorization using granular URL filtering rules.
Reduce the number of uncategorized domains with the help of inline AI/ML-based content categorization.
Quickly identify new domains (Registered, Observed, and Revived).
Block or caution users with specific End User Notifications (EUNs).

blocks.text: The URL Filtering policy rules can also be applied to IoT devices from a location or a sublocation that has the Enforce IoT Policy Control option enabled. You can apply the rules to IoT devices that are identified and classified (e.g., Printers, Sensors) by the Zscaler AI/ML under the IoT group in the Device Groups criterion.

Zscaler provides the Allow Unauthenticated Traffic for IoT Classifications predefined rule for the URL Filtering policy. You can enable this rule to temporarily allow unauthenticated traffic that could be blocked by other rules, so that the Zscaler AI/ML can classify devices. This rule is disabled by default and cannot be deleted. You can modify the Rule Order, Rule Status, Rule Label, and Description for this rule and cannot edit other attributes.

You can create rules that block or caution users and associate them with specific EUNs. For example, your organization has two networks and they each have a web server that hosts an EUN. You can create two different rules that redirect users to the appropriate EUN.

The EUNs that you specify in the rules take precedence over the default EUN that you configure on the Administration > End User Notification > End User Notifications page. Therefore, when a user is blocked or warned due to a rule that is associated with an EUN, the service displays the EUN associated with the rule and not the default EUN.
When you configure a rule, you can specify one of the following actions:

blocks.item: Allow: The service allows access to the URLs in the selected categories. You can still restrict access by specifying a daily quota for bandwidth and time. For example, you can allow your users to access Entertainment and Recreation sites, but restrict the bandwidth allowed for these sites so they don't interfere with business-critical applications. The daily time quota is based on the time that the rule is created. For example, if the rule is created at 11:00 AM PST, then the quota is renewed at 11:00 AM PST the next day.

Caution: When a user tries to access a site, the service displays a Caution notification. You can use the system-defined notification, customize the text, or create your own notification and direct users to it.
See image.
Block: The service displays a Block notification. You can use the system-defined notification, customize the text, or create your own notification and direct users to it.
See image.

Additionally, you can allow some users or groups to override the block with the Allow Override option. For example, you can block students from accessing YouTube but allow the teachers. Teachers are prompted to enter their override password. This can be company-provided credentials such as single sign-on credentials or hosted database credentials based on the Enable Identity-based Block Override settings. Permitted users are allowed to access the blocked page only during their current browser session. They are required to reauthenticate when they try to access it in another browser session.
See image.
Isolate: The service isolates all the traffic to the URLs in the selected categories through a remote browser.

blocks.heading: About the URL Filtering Policy Page

blocks.text: On the URL Filtering Policy page (Internet Access > Policy > URL Filtering), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Click Recommended Policy to view the policy Zscaler recommends.
Configure a URL Filtering rule.
Filter the URL Filtering rule by different criteria (e.g., Rule Label).
Search for a URL Filtering rule.
Select the column options to view the URL Filtering rules accordingly.
View a list of all configured URL Filtering policy rules. For each policy rule, you can view the details.
Policy Rule Details
Rule Order: The policy rule order number. URL Filtering policy rules are evaluated in ascending numerical order. You can sort this column.
The evaluation of the policy rules stops at the first match.
Admin Rank: The admin rank for this rule. This is only visible if you have enabled it in the Advanced Settings. You can sort this column.
Rule Name: The name of the policy rule. You can sort this column.
URL Categories: The URL categories of the policy rule, if available.
URL Categories (AND): The additional URL categories of the policy rule, if available.
The URL Categories fields are connected with a logical AND operator.
Users: The users of the policy rule, if available.
Groups: The groups of the policy rule, if available.
Groups (AND): The additional groups of the policy rule, if available.
Groups (AND): The additional groups of the policy rule, if available.
The Groups fields are connected with a logical AND operator.
Departments: The departments of the policy rule, if available.
Locations: The locations of the policy rule, if available.
Location Groups: The location groups of the policy rule, if available.
Time: The time period during which the policy rule applies, if available.
User Risk Profile: The user risk profile of the policy rule, if available.
Adaptive Access Profile: The adaptive access profile of the policy rule, if available.
Device Trust Level: The device trust level of the policy rule, if available.
Device Groups: The device groups of the policy rule, if available.
Devices: The devices of the policy rule, if available.
Source IP Groups: The source IP groups of the policy rule, if available.
Source Country: The source countries of the policy rule, if available.
Protocol: The protocols of the policy rule, if available.
Request Methods: The request methods of the policy rule, if available.
HTTP Header Profiles: The HTTP header profiles of the policy rule, if available.
User Agent: The user agents of the policy rule, if available.
Workload Groups: The workload groups of the policy rule, if available.
Start Date and Time: The start date and time of the policy rule, if available. The rule is valid starting this date and time.
End Date and Time: The end date and time of the policy rule, if available. The rule ceases to be valid on this date and time.
Time Zone: The time zone in which the policy rule is valid.
Action: Displays whether the policy rule is disabled or whether it's set to Allow, Caution, Block, or Isolate.
The Isolate action is available only if Zero Trust Browser (formerly Isolation) is enabled for your organization.
Labels: The labels of the policy rule, if available.
Description: The description of the policy rule, if available.
Edit, duplicate, or delete a URL Filtering policy rule.
The URL Filtering rules are paginated with up to 500 rules displayed per page.
